item.description:
Fast again after days of use

  • Pastel no longer slows down the longer it runs. A Library or Front Page you had closed kept working in the background after every copy, and that work grew over days until opening the ribbon could take seconds. Closed windows now rest until you open them again.
  • The ribbon opens faster: it no longer reads every item's thumbnail again each time you open it, only the cards you see.

Less disk space

  • Settings › General › Keep History shows how much space Pastel takes on this Mac, including pinboards and saved links.
  • Copying a file no longer saves a picture of it alongside, which was often around 10 MB each. Pasting a file only ever used its location. Copies of the same image saved under older clipboard names are gone too.
  • Pictures saved with earlier file copies go as your history expires.

Saved links

  • Deleting a saved link, or a whole collection, now sticks: the daily update from Zen no longer saves the tab again while it's still in Zen's sidebar.
  • Once you close that tab in Zen, opening the page there again later saves it again.

Choose the display

  • The ribbon can open on a display of your choice: the one under the pointer (as before), the main display, or a specific display by name, like the built-in one with the notch. Set it in Settings › General › Ribbon › Display.
  • If the chosen display isn't connected, the ribbon opens under the pointer, and Settings keeps your choice for when it's back.
  • Hovering over the notch only opens the ribbon on the chosen display.

A fuller Quick Start

  • Two ways to paste: pick where the ribbon opens from five small screens and see it with Show Me, turn on opening by hovering over the notch, and set Pocket's shortcut. With more than one display, choose which one the ribbon uses.
  • Try your first paste now has a step for Pocket, which ticks off once you've pasted with it.
  • More to explore has its own page with what Pastel can do beyond the basics: the big preview, Quick Paste, Paste Stack, saved links and the Front Page, your browser's tabs, the Library, Spaces, smart pinboards, pinboard packs, on-device suggestions, Sync and privacy.
  • Open Quick Start any time from the menu bar.

Put the ribbon where you want it

  • Choose where the ribbon opens in Settings › General › Ribbon, or from the ribbon's ⋯ menu: Bottom (as before), Top, Notch, Left or Right.
  • Notch hangs a shelf from the camera notch, about four cards wide, that grows out of the notch when it opens. On a display without a notch, it hangs from the top center.
  • Top spans the screen over the menu bar, with the cards starting below the notch.
  • Left and Right show a column of cards down the side of the screen, with their own width. ↑ and ↓ move through them.
  • Drag the ribbon's inner edge to resize it in any position. The preview opens beside the ribbon, and confirmations move below a ribbon at the top.
  • Open by hovering over the notch (off by default): rest the pointer on the notch, or the top center of a display without one, to open a ribbon at the top. It closes when the pointer leaves, unless you click it.

Faster with big copies

  • The ribbon opens right away even when you've just copied something huge, like a long base64 string. Before, it could take a third of a second every time.
  • Copying very large text no longer makes Pastel stall for a moment.
  • The preview keeps its full size on a display to the left of your main one.
